newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar vols jump after dlr/yen skids.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar vols jump after dlr/yen skids.

text.p: Another downdraft in the dollar pushed implied volatilities on dollar/yen options sharply higher in U.S. trading, traders said.
The dollar shed two full yen in Europe, falling as low as 114.70 yen as worries intensified that Japan will raise the official discount rate. At the U.S. midday, it had recovered to 115.90 yen.
Although opinions were mixed about where the dollar was headed next, the rising volatilities, especially in shorter dates, reflected a general view that it was not about to take a rest, traders said.

"It is unlikely the market will stabilize around here soon," said Masao Okada, chief dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank. With Japanese interest rates pushing higher, narrowing the differential with U.S. and European rates, economic fundamentals suggest 110 to 120 yen may be an appropriate range for the dollar, he said.

Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen climbed to 11.6/11.7 percent, compared with 10.5/10.9 percent Wednesday, after reaching as high as 12.4 percent this morning in London, U.S. traders said. Two-month dollar/yen volatility was 10.7/10.9 percent and six-month was 9.9/10.1 percent.
Dollar/yen risk reversals for 25-delta options remained skewed toward yen calls at 1.2/1.4, continuing the strong bias that emerged Friday when the dollar began its free-fall.

Some market participants were looking to buy dips in dollar/yen volatility, traders said. They noted that financing the premium on those purchases by selling dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss volatility was a popular strategy.

Those who are dollar bearish were buying dollar puts and yen calls out one to three months, but some longer-term dollar bulls were still buying six-month to one-year dollar calls and yen puts, traders said.
In addition, traders said, Japanese trust funds and securities firms were still trying to hedge downside dollar risk, and were buying short-dated dollar puts and yen calls in 113 and 115 strikes.
Dollar/mark volatility was 9.0/9.3 percent for one-month options, up from 8.6/9.0 percent Wednesday. Two-year was 8.9/9.1 percent and six-month was 8.85/9.0.
One-month 25-delta risk reversals for dollar/mark were unchanged from the previous session at flat/0.3 in favor of mark calls.
